en: summary, general outline; (개괄하다) to summarize, give a general outline

examples.en: I summarized the meeting content in broad outline and reported it.

examples.ko: 신문 기사는 첫 문단에서 사건 전체를 개괄하고 뒤에서 세부를 설명한다.
examples.en: A news article outlines the whole event in the first paragraph and explains the details later.

examples.ko: 발표자는 먼저 지난 분기의 실적을 간단히 개괄했습니다.
examples.en: The presenter first gave a brief overview of last quarter's results.

examples.ko: 연구 결과의 개괄을 한 장으로 정리해 달라는 요청을 받았어요.
examples.en: I got a request to put the overview of the research results on one page.

examples.ko: 이 장에서는 한국 경제의 흐름을 개괄하고, 다음 장에서 각 업종을 살펴보겠습니다.
examples.en: This chapter outlines the course of the Korean economy, and the next chapter looks at each industry.

explain: 개괄(槪括)은 중요한 내용만 뽑아 전체를 간단히 정리하는 것이에요. '개괄하다'로 써요. 글이나 발표에서 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '요약'이나 '간단히 말하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 개괄 (槪括) is picking out the main points and summing up the whole briefly. It is used as 개괄하다 in writing and presentations. In everyday talk, 요약 or 간단히 말하다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: I had an argument with my friend over a small thing.

examples.ko: 말싸움 끝에 둘 다 화가 나서 가 버렸어요.
examples.en: After the argument, both of them got angry and left.
The siblings argue often, so their parents worry.
Even if you win an argument, you don't feel good.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 말싸움이 벌어져서 분위기가 나빠졌어요.
examples.en: A quarrel broke out during the meeting and the mood turned bad.
It started as an argument but ended in a big fight.

explain: 말로만 다투는 것이 '말싸움'이고, 몸으로 때리며 싸우는 것은 '몸싸움'이에요. '말다툼'과 거의 같은 말이에요. '말싸움을 하다', '말싸움이 벌어지다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I had an argument with my younger sibling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말싸움'과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 둘 다 일상에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 말싸움, and both are common in daily speech.

phrases.en: An argument broke out during the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 말싸움이 시작되었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an argument suddenly starts.

phrases.example: 저는 형과 말싸움에서 한 번도 못 이겨요.
phrases.en: I never win an argument with my older brother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말싸움의 결과를 말할 때 '이기다, 지다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 이기다 and 지다 to talk about who wins or loses an argument.

explain_en: A fight with words only is a 말싸움, while a physical fight is a 몸싸움. It's almost the same as 말다툼. Say '말싸움을 하다' or '말싸움이 벌어지다'.

examples.en: I want to learn business English.

examples.ko: 출장 가서 비즈니스석을 처음 타 봤어요.
examples.en: On a business trip I rode in business class for the first time.
My friend started a small business.

examples.ko: 비즈니스 메일은 짧고 분명하게 써야 해요.
examples.en: Business emails should be written short and clear.

examples.ko: 비즈니스 파트너를 만나러 다음 주에 부산에 가요.
examples.en: I'm going to Busan next week to meet a business partner.

examples.ko: 이 호텔은 비즈니스 손님이 많이 와요.
examples.en: This hotel gets a lot of business guests.

explain: 회사와 돈이 오가는 일을 넓게 부를 때 쓰는 외래어예요. 내가 직접 꾸리는 일은 '사업', 회사에서 맡은 일은 '업무'나 '일'이라서 자리가 달라요. 비즈니스는 영어·메일·호텔처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I'm learning business English to use at work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일할 때 쓰는 영어를 말할 때 '비즈니스'를 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: '비즈니스' goes in front to name English used at work.

phrases.en: You should write business emails politely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사 사람이나 고객에게 보내는 일 관련 메일을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to work-related emails sent to colleagues or clients.

phrases.en: I booked a business hotel for my business trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 출장 온 사람이 많이 묵는 간단하고 깔끔한 호텔을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple, tidy hotel often used by people on business trips.

explain_en: A loanword for work that involves companies and money in a broad sense. A venture you run yourself is '사업' and the tasks you handle at a company are '업무' or '일', so they fill different slots. 'Business' often sits in front of other words, such as English, email or hotel.

examples.en: My older sister is getting promoted this month.
My father was promoted to department head last year.
If you work hard, you can be promoted.
I was promoted and my pay went up a lot too.
What changes if you get promoted?
I got promoted and moved to a new office.

explain: 직장에서 직급이 올라갈 때만 써요. 월급만 오른 경우는 '월급이 오르다'라고 해요. 새 직급 뒤에 '(으)로'를 붙여서 '과장으로 승진하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 김 대리가 다음 달에 과장으로 승진해요.
phrases.en: Assistant Manager Kim is being promoted to manager next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 직급 뒤에 '(으)로'를 붙여서 어떤 자리로 올라가는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put (으)로 after the new rank to say which position someone is promoted to.

phrases.example: 저는 열심히 일해서 빨리 승진하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to work hard and get promoted quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여서 바라는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -고 싶다 expresses a wish or hope.

phrases.en: Congratulations on your promotion, Minsu!
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '승진'에 조사를 붙여, 다른 사람의 좋은 일을 축하할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 승진 with a particle to congratulate someone.

explain_en: Use it only when your rank at work goes up. If only your pay rises, say '월급이 오르다'. The new rank takes '(으)로', as in '과장으로 승진하다'.

examples.ko: 저희 부모님은 대학에서 만나 연애결혼을 하셨어요.
examples.en: My parents met at university and had a love marriage.

examples.ko: 저는 소개로 만나는 것보다 연애결혼이 좋아요.
examples.en: I prefer a love marriage to meeting through an introduction.
I heard that in the old days few people had love marriages.
Even couples who had a love marriage sometimes argue a lot.

examples.ko: 연애결혼이든 소개로 만나든 서로 맞추는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: Whether you had a love marriage or met through an introduction, adjusting to each other matters.
After dating for three years, they had a love marriage.

explain: 서로 사귀다가 결혼하는 걸 말하고, 반대는 '중매결혼'이에요. 소개로 만나 결혼하는 경우는 '맞선을 보고 결혼했다'처럼 말하기도 해요. '연애결혼을 하다'와 '연애결혼하다' 둘 다 써요.

phrases.en: My older sister had a love marriage last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연애결혼을 하다'를 붙여 한 동사처럼 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A one-verb form of 'yeonaegyeolhoneul hada'.

phrases.en: My grandmother had an arranged marriage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연애결혼의 반대말이에요. 둘을 비교할 때 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of a love marriage; used when comparing the two.

phrases.en: My parents had a love marriage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼 방식을 설명할 때 '이에요/이었어요'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'ieyo/ieosseoyo' to explain how a couple married.

explain_en: It means dating first and then marrying, and the opposite is '중매결혼' (arranged marriage). For meeting through an introduction you may hear '맞선을 보고 결혼했다' (married after a formal matchmaking meeting). Both '연애결혼을 하다' and '연애결혼하다' are used.

en: to admit; to acknowledge; to recognize

examples.en: I honestly admitted that I was wrong.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 맛을 인정받아서 손님이 늘었어요.
examples.en: This shop's taste got recognized, so it has more customers.
Everyone acknowledges that person's skill.
Admitting my mistake was not as easy as I thought.

examples.ko: 상대 팀도 우리가 이겼다고 인정하지 않았어요.
examples.en: The other team did not admit that we had won either.
I want to work hard and be recognized at my company.

explain: '인정하다'는 잘못이나 사실을 '맞다'고 받아들일 때 써요. 내가 하면 '인정하다', 남에게 능력을 알아봐 주는 말을 들으면 '인정받다'라고 해요. 반대말은 '부인하다'예요.

phrases.en: My skills were recognized at work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 나를 좋게 알아줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when others recognize and value you.

phrases.en: He doesn't admit his mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사실이나 잘못을 받아들이지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone won't accept a fact or fault.

phrases.en: My teacher acknowledged my effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람의 노력이나 능력을 알아줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you acknowledge someone else's effort or ability.

explain_en: '인정하다' is used when you accept that a mistake or fact is true. When you do it, it is '인정하다'; when others recognize your ability, it is '인정받다'. The opposite is '부인하다' (to deny).

dis.h: everyday; accept as true, or recognize ability

p.n: The other word is more formal and fits only admitting a fault.

en: to get a job; to be hired; to be employed

examples.en: I graduate this year and get a job right away.
My older brother got a job at a bank last year.
I want to get a job soon.
Getting a job isn't easy these days.

examples.ko: 한국 회사에 취직하면 비자를 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you get a job at a Korean company, you can get a visa.
After I got a job, I gave my parents a gift.

explain: '취직하다'는 직장을 얻는 순간을 말하고, 이미 일하는 상태는 '일하다'나 '다니다'로 말해요. '회사에 다녀요'가 '회사에 취직해요'보다 지금 상태에 맞아요. '취업하다'도 비슷한데, 일자리를 얻는 일 전체에 더 넓게 써요.

phrases.en: I got a job at a company last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 일자리를 얻은 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used for having gotten a job.

phrases.en: I want to get a job quickly after I graduate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '취직하다'와 뜻이 같지만 '을 하다'로 나누어 말하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 취직하다, but split into 취직 plus 을 하다.

phrases.en: My friend is preparing to find a job these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일자리를 구하려고 준비하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for preparing to find a job.

explain_en: 취직하다 is the moment you land a job, while the ongoing state is '일하다' or '다니다' ('회사에 다녀요' fits better than '회사에 취직해요' for now). '취업하다' is close but covers getting work more broadly.

examples.en: This song is the biggest hit of the year.
That movie was a big hit.
To become a hit product, price matters too.
The singer has many hit songs, so I look forward to the concert.
This new product is sure to be a hit.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 히트 노래를 다 외웠어요.
examples.en: I memorized all of that singer's hit songs.

explain: '히트를 치다'처럼 '치다'와 함께 나오는 일이 많아서 '히트하다'보다 '히트를 치다'를 더 자주 들어요. '히트 상품', '히트곡', '히트작'처럼 앞뒤에 말을 붙여서도 많이 써요. '인기', '대박'과 비슷하지만 노래·영화·상품에 주로 써요.

phrases.example: 그 가수의 새 노래가 히트를 쳤어요.
phrases.en: The singer's new song became a hit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '히트'와 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 말로, 크게 성공했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing with 'hit', meaning something became a big success.

phrases.example: 이 노래는 그 가수의 최고 히트곡이에요.
phrases.en: This song is that singer's biggest hit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '히트' 뒤에 '곡'을 붙여서 크게 인기를 얻은 노래를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'song' after 'hit' gives a word for a hugely popular song.

phrases.en: This snack is this year's hit product.
phrases.nuance_ko: '히트' 뒤에 '상품'을 붙여서 아주 잘 팔리는 물건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'product' after 'hit' names an item that sells very well.

explain_en: It often appears with 치다, so people hear 히트를 치다 more often than 히트하다. It also combines easily, as in 히트 상품, 히트곡, and 히트작. It is close to 인기 or 대박 but mainly applies to songs, films, and products.
